Repo: C:/Projects/DS/DS_Communication (Windows, git repo). Review target: commit 8159042 — get the diff with `git show 8159042` (or `git diff 8159042~1 8159042`). It is a from-scratch rewrite of a connection-oriented network transport library in C#: Communication.Shared (Session / MessagePipeline / Framing / Threading contracts, netstandard2.1) + Communication.Network.TCP + xUnit tests (Test/Communication.Tests) + Sandbox/Chat.TCP sample. Design contracts the code must honor live in Document/ — read at minimum Document/01-Overview/Feature-Spec.md (spec + runtime-contract decisions), Document/03-Reference/Public-API.md, Document/02-Architecture/Pipeline.md, Document/02-Architecture/Session.md. HARD RULES: you are READ-ONLY — do not edit, create, or delete any file. Work from actual files and commands, not assumptions. Report findings as a ranked list. Each finding: SEVERITY [BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR] | file:line | what is wrong (evidence from code) | concrete suggested fix. Only report issues you verified in the code — no speculation, no style nits. Keep the whole report under ~120 lines. If you find nothing in some category, say so explicitly.

YOUR ANGLE: speed — allocations and throughput of hot paths, GC pressure matters (Unity/netstandard2.1 consumers). Focus areas: (1) send hot path — PooledBufferWriter growth strategy, per-batch List reuse, coalesce limit overshoot, semaphore/gate wait churn, whether frames are copied more than necessary; (2) receive hot path — per-frame ArrayPool rent/return, header buffer reuse, deserialize span lifetime, dispatch queue boxing/allocations; (3) message-channel receive callback path (fire-and-forget ValueTask, allocation per message); (4) SignalGate / SemaphoreSlim wait allocation patterns; (5) anything O(n^2) or lock-heavy under many sessions; (6) TCP layer — StreamByteChannel Task/ValueTask wrapping, listener accept cost. Compare against the legacy expectations in Document/ (coalesce ~64KB, ArrayPool use). Rank by impact-per-fix-effort.
summary:
## Review — commit 8159042, angle: allocations & throughput of hot paths

Read: `MessagePipeline.cs`, `PooledBufferWriter.cs`, `SignalGate.cs`, framing, TCP layer, plus `Feature-Spec.md`, `Public-API.md`, `Pipeline.md`, `Session.md`, legacy `Data-Flow.md` for parity. Static analysis only; tests not executed (read-only rule — `dotnet test` writes bin/obj).

**Ranked findings (impact-per-fix-effort):**

1. **MAJOR** | `Source/Communication.Shared/Framing/LengthPrefixFrameReader.cs:31,48` + `Messages/MessagePipeline.cs:289-299` | Receive path does ≥2 channel reads per frame: an exact 4-byte header read (`ReadExactOrZeroAsync(_header.AsMemory())`), then a separate body `ReadExactAsync`. The sender deliberately coalesces many small frames into one write, but the receiver pays 2 kernel reads per small message (e.g. a 64KB coalesced batch of ~100B chat messages ≈ 1280 reads vs ~1). No accumulation buffer exists anywhere on the receive path. This matches the legacy flow (`Legacy/Document/02-Architecture/Data-Flow.md` §TCP 수신), so it is an inherited ceiling, not a regression — but it is the single biggest throughput lever for small-message workloads. **Fix:** give the receive loop a persistent sliding buffer (rent one ~16–64KB ArrayPool buffer, `ReadAsync` into free space, slice frames out; fall back to per-frame rent only for frames larger than the buffer).

2. **MINOR** | `Source/Communication.Shared/Messages/MessagePipeline.cs:231-234` and `405-413` | Per-item `_sendSlots.Release()` / `_receiveSlots.Release()` after a batch. `SemaphoreSlim.Release` takes its internal Monitor unconditionally, so a drained batch of N messages costs N lock acquisitions (N can be hundreds per 64KB batch). **Fix:** keep the per-item `Flush?.TrySetResult` loop, but hoist the releases to one `_sendSlots.Release(_batch.Count)` (and a counter for `_receiveSlots.Release(count)`). Trivial diff, removes the only per-message lock on the happy path.
